summary: Iteration 15 — Validation du fix VPS deploy #2 (requirements.txt regénéré). Tous les checks passent : (1) grep OK — APScheduler, tzlocal, pdf2image, pytest-asyncio, websocket-client présents ; aucune ligne 'litellm @ http' ; 132 lignes. (2) Simulation Docker build via venv vierge : pip install -r requirements.txt --extra-index-url https://d33sy5i8bnduwe.cloudfront.net/simple/ réussit (litellm-1.80.0 installé transitivement par emergentintegrations-0.2.0). (3) `python -c 'import server'` depuis /app/backend => IMPORT_SERVER_OK. (4) `import litellm, apscheduler, tzlocal, pdf2image` OK. (5) Régression backend pod : 3/3 pytest pass (health, admin login, superadmin login + /api/admin/tenants liste Logitrak).
critical_code_review_comments: requirements.txt now uses `pip freeze` output (fixed pins). This ensures reproducibility on the VPS Docker build but freezes transitive dependency versions — future dependency upgrades will require another regen. Acceptable trade-off for deployment stability.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_15 validated the VPS deployment fix #2. requirements.txt is 132 lines, no `litellm @ http` line, contains APScheduler/tzlocal/pdf2image/pytest-asyncio/websocket-client. Clean venv install + `import server` reproduces IMPORT_SERVER_OK (same as Dockerfile behavior on VPS). Backend pod regression (health + admin + superadmin + /api/admin/tenants) 3/3 pass. Iteration_13 multi-tenant (14/14) and iteration_14 yarn.lock (5/5) remain green. Ready to redeploy on VPS.
rca of the issue: Root cause was that /app/backend/requirements.txt had not been regenerated after apscheduler/tzlocal/pdf2image/pytest-asyncio/websocket-client were pip-installed inside the pod, so the Docker build on the VPS was missing them → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'apscheduler'` at `from apscheduler...` in /app/backend/app/scheduler.py:15, causing container restart loop. Fix: regenerated requirements.txt via `pip freeze` (132 lignes) excluding the direct `litellm @ https://...` line (litellm is pulled transitively via emergentintegrations). Validated by clean venv install + `import server` — no errors.
